title: Radio Properties of RS Canum Venaticorum Variables in VLASS and RACS
comment: 26 pages, 12 figures, 2 MRT tables (Tables 2 & 3), Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We performed a systematic search for radio emission from RS Canum Venaticorum (RS CVn) binaries, selected from the International Variable Star Index (VSX) catalog, in the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS; three epochs) and Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS; two epochs) data. We detected 108 candidate radio-emitting RS CVn in at least one epoch. Several of these systems rank among the most radio-luminous RS CVn binaries reported to date. The radio and X-ray luminosities, obtained from cross-matching with the eROSITA and ROSAT X-ray catalogs, are consistent with the Guedel-Benz relation for magnetically active stars, but are also comparable to radio-luminous quiescent black hole X-ray binaries, indicating a potential for misidentification between these two classes. Analysis of optical, radio, and stellar properties indicates that optically bright RS CVn (i.e., those with at least one giant component) are radio-quieter and have periods that are consistent with lower coronal activity. However, two of these optically bright RS CVn systems show persistent and unusually high radio specific luminosities (>2e17 erg/s/Hz) across all observed epochs, showing that stellar activity can produce relatively persistent radio signals as bright as quiescent black hole binaries.

AI.tldr: The paper systematically searches for radio emission from RS CVn binary systems in VLASS and RACS survey data, detecting 108 candidate radio-emitting systems. It finds their radio/X-ray luminosities follow the Guedel-Benz relation for magnetically active stars but are comparable to radio-luminous quiescent black hole X-ray binaries, posing a potential misidentification risk, and identifies two optically bright systems with persistent, unusually high radio luminosity.
AI.motivation: RS CVn binaries are magnetically active systems that can emit radio signals bright enough to be mistaken for quiescent black hole X-ray binaries. No systematic, multi-epoch survey of radio emission from a large sample of RS CVn systems had been conducted, leaving the frequency, luminosity distribution, and potential for source misclassification poorly characterized.
AI.method: The authors systematically searched radio emission from RS CVn binaries (selected from the VSX catalog) across three epochs of VLASS and two epochs of RACS survey data. They cross-matched detected radio sources with eROSITA and ROSAT X-ray catalogs, and analyzed optical, radio, and stellar properties of the detected systems.
AI.result: 108 candidate radio-emitting RS CVn systems were detected in at least one epoch, with several among the most radio-luminous known. Radio and X-ray luminosities are consistent with the Guedel-Benz relation for magnetically active stars but comparable to quiescent black hole X-ray binaries. Optically bright RS CVn (with at least one giant component) are radio-quieter with lower coronal activity indicators, yet two such systems exhibit persistent, unusually high radio luminosities (>2e17 erg/s/Hz) across all epochs.
AI.conclusion: Radio-emitting RS CVn binaries can reach luminosities comparable to quiescent black hole X-ray binaries, highlighting a significant potential for misidentification between these source classes. Stellar magnetic activity in specific RS CVn systems can produce persistent bright radio emission, necessitating careful discrimination criteria in future radio surveys.

title: H-$α$ Integral Carrington Synoptic Maps Produced by NSO/NISP
summary: Monitoring long-term chromospheric activity and large-scale solar structures like filaments and plages is critical for understanding solar magnetic cycles and predicting space-weather events. While photospheric magnetic fields are routinely mapped, a consistent, global reference for chromospheric structures has been absent from H-$α$ observations. This technical report provides a comprehensive description of the methodology used to construct the NSF Global Oscillations Network Group (GONG) H-$α$ Integral Carrington Synoptic Maps from full-disk observations. We outline the processing pipeline developed to transform these observations into 720 x 360 pixel maps binned by Carrington longitude and sine(latitude) and describe characteristics of the final data product.

AI.tldr: This technical report details the methodology for constructing the GONG H-α Integral Carrington Synoptic Maps, a new global reference for chromospheric structures, describing the processing pipeline that converts full-disk observations into 720×360 pixel maps binned by Carrington longitude and sine(latitude).
AI.motivation: Monitoring chromospheric activity and large-scale solar structures is critical for understanding solar magnetic cycles and space-weather prediction, yet no consistent global reference for chromospheric structures existed in H-α observations, unlike the routinely mapped photospheric magnetic fields.
AI.method: A processing pipeline transforms full-disk H-α observations from the GONG network into 720×360 pixel Integral Carrington Synoptic Maps, binned by Carrington longitude and sine(latitude).
AI.result: The final data product is a set of chromospheric synoptic maps with defined spatial binning and documented characteristics, establishing a consistent global reference for H-α observations.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a comprehensive methodological description and characterization of the GONG H-α Integral Carrington Synoptic Maps, filling the gap in global chromospheric reference data for solar cycle and space-weather studies.

title: A chemo-dynamical search for planet-candidate hosts of possible extragalactic origin
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: To date, all known exoplanetary systems have been identified around stars currently residing in the Milky Way, whereas planets formed in external galaxies remain largely unexplored. Such systems would offer a unique probe of planet formation in galactic environments distinct from the Milky Way. We combine a literature-compiled sample of Kepler, K2, and TESS planet-candidate host stars with Gaia DR3 astrometry and radial velocities, and incorporate metallicities and [Mg/Fe] abundances from the LAMOST DR9 DD-Payne catalogue, to search for candidate accreted-halo planet hosts. We identify 11 planet-candidate hosts with halo-like kinematics, five of which have reliable chemical abundance measurements. Among these, four systems exhibit low metallicities ([Fe/H]<-0.7) and low [Mg/Fe] ratios that are inconsistent with the canonical Milky Way thick-disc sequence, indicative of enrichment histories characteristic of accreted dwarf galaxies. We further carry out a uniform false-positive assessment using Gaia RUWE, Gaia DR3 neighbourhood checks, odd--even transit-depth comparisons, secondary-eclipse searches, independent BLS period recovery, and comparison with ExoFOP and available follow-up information. This vetting identifies EPIC~211407755 and TIC~239541449 as the most plausible, although still unvalidated, planet-candidate systems. TIC~293432942 is more likely associated with a blended or otherwise binary-related false positive, whereas TIC~184739529 remains a high-risk giant-companion candidate whose planetary nature is uncertain. If confirmed, EPIC~211407755 and TIC~239541449 would suggest that planetary systems can form in dwarf-galaxy environments and subsequently survive accretion into the Milky Way.

AI.tldr: A search for exoplanet-host stars with accreted-halo kinematics reveals 11 candidates, with EPIC 211407755 and TIC 239541449 emerging as the most plausible (though unvalidated) planet-hosting systems. Their low metallicity and low [Mg/Fe] abundances suggest they originated in accreted dwarf galaxies, implying planets can form and survive in extragalactic environments.
AI.motivation: All known exoplanet systems reside around stars in the Milky Way, leaving planets formed in external galaxies unexplored. Such systems would provide unique constraints on planet formation in galactic environments distinct from our own.
AI.method: Combined Kepler, K2, and TESS planet-candidate host stars with Gaia DR3 astrometry and radial velocities, LAMOST DR9 DD-Payne metallicities and [Mg/Fe] abundances. Identified stars with halo-like kinematics, then performed uniform false-positive vetting including Gaia RUWE, neighbourhood checks, odd-even transit-depth comparisons, secondary-eclipse searches, BLS period recovery, and comparison with ExoFOP and follow-up data.
AI.result: Identified 11 planet-candidate hosts with halo-like kinematics, five with reliable chemistry. Four show low metallicity and low [Mg/Fe] inconsistent with the Milky Way thick-disc sequence, pointing to accreted dwarf-galaxy origins. Vetting identified EPIC 211407755 and TIC 239541449 as the most plausible candidates; TIC 293432942 is likely a blended/binary false positive, and TIC 184739529 remains uncertain.
AI.conclusion: If confirmed, the candidates would demonstrate that planetary systems can form in dwarf-galaxy environments and survive subsequent accretion into the Milky Way, opening a new window on extra-Milky-Way planet formation.

title: Evidence for Dynamical Filtering: High Binary Fraction, Hard-binary Excess, and Unresolved Triples in the Surviving Core of NGC 6791
summary: We present a deep photometric analysis of the main-sequence (MS) population in the old, metal-rich open cluster (OC) NGC 6791 using Gaia Data Release 3 data. After correcting for differential reddening, we use the Bayesian model comparison to test whether stellar rotation can account for the observed MS broadening and find that a rotation-dominated interpretation is strongly disfavored. We therefore infer that unresolved multiplicity is the primary contributor to the photometric offsets. We derive a high-q companion fraction of $54.3\% \pm 2.8\%$ for systems with $q \gtrsim 0.5$, significantly higher than typical values reported for most OCs and the field. The inferred offset distribution is not consistent with a flat mass-ratio distribution but instead shows an excess toward high mass ratios ($q \sim 0.8$--$1.0$), suggestive of preferential survival of hard binaries in a dynamically evolved environment. We also identify a population of stars lying above the equal-mass binary limit ($ΔG > 0.75$ mag), which is difficult to explain with ordinary MS binaries alone and is plausibly interpreted as candidate unresolved triple or higher-order multiple systems. A Kolmogorov--Smirnov test, together with Monte Carlo label-shuffling experiments, shows no statistically significant difference between the projected radial distributions of the single-star and binary/multiple populations within the observed field. Taken together, these results are consistent with the picture that NGC 6791 is the dynamically processed inner remnant of a once more massive cluster.

AI.tldr: Using Gaia DR3 photometry of the old, metal-rich open cluster NGC 6791, the authors rule out stellar rotation as the cause of main-sequence broadening, attribute it to unresolved multiplicity, and derive a high companion fraction of 54.3% for q≥0.5 with an excess toward high mass ratios, plus a population of candidate triple/higher-order systems. No radial segregation between single and multiple stars is found, supporting the interpretation of NGC 6791 as a dynamically processed cluster remnant.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origin of main-sequence broadening in NGC 6791, distinguishing between stellar rotation and unresolved multiplicity, and to characterize the binary/multiple star population in this old, metal-rich cluster.
AI.method: Deep photometric analysis of Gaia DR3 data with differential reddening correction; Bayesian model comparison to test rotation vs. multiplicity; mass-ratio distribution inference; Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and Monte Carlo label-shuffling for radial distribution comparisons.
AI.result: Rotation-dominated interpretation is strongly disfavored; high-q companion fraction of 54.3%±2.8%; offset distribution shows excess at q~0.8-1.0; a population above the equal-mass binary limit (ΔG>0.75 mag) suggests unresolved triples/higher-order systems; no significant radial segregation between single and multiple stars.
AI.conclusion: NGC 6791 is likely the dynamically processed inner remnant of a once more massive cluster, with unresolved multiplicity dominating the main-sequence broadening and hard binaries preferentially surviving.

title: High-order Paschen emission from the quiet-Sun off-limb chromosphere
summary: We report the detection of high-order hydrogen Paschen emission lines (Pa~15, Pa~16, and Pa~17) in the quiet-Sun chromosphere off the solar limb using the Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) on board the {\sc Sunrise~iii} balloon telescope. These lines reveal thread-like structures resembling spicules and exhibit systematically smaller Doppler velocities than Ca~II~854.2~nm, suggesting that they are optically thinner and more affected by line-of-sight averaging, especially near the limb. Non-LTE radiative transfer synthesis using the spherically symmetric one-dimensional code \texttt{rhsphere} reproduces the overall spectral properties. The observed ratios among three Paschen lines show systematic deviations from synthetic and theoretical results, suggesting that additional physical effects may influence the formation of high-order Paschen lines. The study demonstrates the potential of high-order Paschen lines as a new diagnostic of optically thin plasma in the off-limb chromosphere.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first detection of high-order hydrogen Paschen emission lines (Pa 15, Pa 16, Pa 17) in the off-limb quiet-Sun chromosphere using the SCIP instrument on the Sunrise III balloon telescope. These lines form thread-like spicule structures with smaller Doppler velocities than Ca II 854.2 nm, indicating optically thinner plasma and line-of-sight averaging effects. Non-LTE 1D spherical radiative transfer modeling (rhsphere) reproduces overall spectral properties, though observed line ratios deviate systematically from predictions, suggesting additional physical effects. The work establishes high-order Paschen lines as new diagnostics for optically thin off-limb chromospheric plasma.
AI.motivation: To explore high-order hydrogen Paschen lines as new diagnostics for optically thin plasma in the off-limb solar chromosphere, where traditional strong lines are optically thick and suffer from complex radiative transfer effects.
AI.method: Spectropolarimetric observations with SCIP on Sunrise III to detect Paschen lines off-limb; comparison with Ca II 854.2 nm Doppler velocities; forward modeling using the spherically symmetric 1D Non-LTE radiative transfer code rhsphere to synthesize and compare spectral profiles and line ratios.
AI.result: Detected Pa 15, Pa 16, and Pa 17 in the off-limb quiet-Sun chromosphere. The lines trace spicule-like thread structures with systematically smaller Doppler velocities than Ca II 854.2 nm. rhsphere reproduces overall spectral properties, but observed ratios among the three Paschen lines deviate systematically from synthetic and theoretical predictions, implying extra physical effects in their formation.
AI.conclusion: High-order Paschen lines hold promise as new diagnostics for optically thin plasma in the off-limb chromosphere, though the systematic discrepancies in line ratios warrant further investigation into additional physical processes affecting their formation.

title: The B-Index as a Diagnostic of Cool Stars: Assessing Metallicity Dependence of TiO Absorption in the Visible Spectrum
summary: Molecular absorption features constitute essential diagnostics of late-type stellar atmospheres, with titanium oxide (TiO) bands serving as sensitive tracers of effective temperature and magnetic activity. While near-infrared TiO indices are well established, visible-band diagnostics provide complementary constraints for stellar classification and parameter estimation. This study investigates the metallicity dependence of the B-index, a TiO absorption measure centered at 567 nm, through synthetic spectra generated with ATLAS9 and high-resolution observations from the HARPS spectrograph. The synthetic grid spans effective temperatures between 3500-4000 K and metallicities from [Fe/H] =-4 to +0.2, while the observational sample comprises 23 MK spectral types stars with effective temperatures between 3500-4000 K. Both theoretical and empirical analyses demonstrate that the B-index exhibits negligible sensitivity to stellar metallicity, with only marginal correlations detected. Therefore, there is no requirement to include this feature in the calculation of the B-index. The B-index's low sensitivity to metallicity reinforces its utility as an effective tool for spectral classification, stellar atmosphere modeling, and the study of magnetically active stars.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the metallicity dependence of the B-index, a TiO absorption measure at 567 nm, using synthetic ATLAS9 spectra and HARPS observations of 23 stars (3500-4000 K, [Fe/H]=-4 to +0.2). Both theoretical and empirical analyses show the B-index has negligible sensitivity to stellar metallicity, confirming its utility for spectral classification and studying magnetically active stars without needing metallicity corrections.
AI.motivation: While near-infrared TiO indices are well established as temperature and magnetic activity tracers, visible-band diagnostics provide complementary constraints for stellar classification. This study aims to determine whether the B-index at 567 nm depends on metallicity, which would affect its reliability and require corrections in stellar parameter estimation.
AI.method: The study uses synthetic spectra generated with ATLAS9 models spanning effective temperatures 3500-4000 K and metallicities from [Fe/H]=-4 to +0.2, combined with high-resolution HARPS spectrograph observations of 23 MK spectral type stars with effective temperatures between 3500-4000 K. Both synthetic and observational samples were analyzed to assess the correlation between the B-index and stellar metallicity.
AI.result: Both theoretical (ATLAS9 synthetic grid) and empirical (HARPS observations) analyses demonstrate that the B-index exhibits negligible sensitivity to stellar metallicity, with only marginal correlations detected across the full metallicity range studied.
AI.conclusion: Since the B-index shows negligible metallicity dependence, no metallicity correction is required when computing this TiO absorption index. Its insensitivity to metallicity reinforces the B-index's value as a robust tool for spectral classification, stellar atmosphere modeling, and studying magnetically active stars.

title: Magnetoacoustic Portals in Quiet-Sun Fluxtubes Revealed by Chromospheric Spectropolarimetry with SUNRISE III/SCIP
summary: Acoustic waves propagate into the chromosphere, contributing to energy transport and their dynamics. Their upward propagation is restricted to frequencies above the acoustic cutoff frequency. The magnetic field configuration plays a key role in determining whether acoustic waves can propagate upward because the cutoff frequency is reduced in regions where the field is inclined with respect to gravity, forming so-called magnetoacoustic portals. Previous studies linked magnetic fields and oscillations in quiet regions, but these analyses were based on photospheric magnetic field information, leaving chromospheric structure unconstrained. This study investigates the coupling between acoustic waves and magnetic topology using photospheric and, for the first time, chromospheric spectropolarimetry in a quiet region, obtained with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) aboard the Sunrise iii balloon-borne solar observatory launched in 2024. The SCIP sit-and-stare observations sampled magnetic features in which the line-of-sight field strength exhibits multiple sharp spatial peaks in the photosphere while becoming broader and weaker at two heights in the chromosphere, indicating expanding fluxtubes. The chromospheric velocity field in these fluxtubes exhibits strong 5-minute oscillations, while the surrounding regions show weak 3-minute oscillations. In these fluxtubes, sawtooth temporal velocity variations are associated with intensity enhancements, suggesting steepened shocks. Fluxtubes with low-frequency oscillations are identified not only in network regions but also in weak internetwork regions. These results provide observational evidence that fluxtubes expanding into the chromosphere act as magnetoacoustic portals, in both network and internetwork regions, allowing low-frequency waves to propagate upward and driving chromospheric dynamics via shocks.

AI.tldr: Using first-ever chromospheric spectropolarimetry (SCIP aboard Sunrise III) alongside photospheric data in a quiet solar region, this study finds observational evidence that expanding magnetic fluxtubes act as magnetoacoustic portals—both in network and internetwork regions—allowing low-frequency (5-minute) acoustic waves to propagate into the chromosphere, where they steepen into shocks and drive chromospheric dynamics.
AI.motivation: Previous studies linked photospheric magnetic fields to oscillations in quiet regions, but chromospheric magnetic structure was unconstrained. Since magnetic field inclination reduces the acoustic cutoff frequency, understanding whether and how fluxtubes enable low-frequency wave propagation upward requires chromospheric magnetic field information, which had been missing.
AI.method: The study used coordinated photospheric and, for the first time, chromospheric spectropolarimetry from the SCIP instrument aboard the Sunrise III balloon-borne observatory (launched 2024). Sit-and-stare observations sampled magnetic features showing multiple sharp photospheric line-of-sight field peaks that broaden and weaken at two chromospheric heights, indicating expanding fluxtubes. Temporal velocity and intensity variations were analyzed within and around these fluxtubes.
AI.result: Chromospheric velocity fields within fluxtubes exhibit strong 5-minute oscillations, while surrounding regions show weak 3-minute oscillations. Inside the fluxtubes, sawtooth temporal velocity variations coincide with intensity enhancements, indicating steepened shocks. Low-frequency oscillating fluxtubes are found in both network and weak internetwork regions.
AI.conclusion: Expanding chromospheric fluxtubes serve as magnetoacoustic portals that lower the acoustic cutoff frequency and permit low-frequency (5-minute) waves to propagate upward through the chromosphere in both network and internetwork regions. These propagating waves steepen into shocks, contributing to energy deposition and driving chromospheric dynamics.
